- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after a spike or recovery.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, particularly when true values show sharp declines or mean reversion.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underreacting to sudden drops or spikes in the true data.
- When true values show a strong downward trend in the last 5–10 days, model forecasts remain stubbornly high.
- Model often fails to capture the “mean reversion” effect after a sharp spike — it holds high values longer than warranted.
- Model overcorrects after a spike, overshooting the true mean and then undercorrecting in subsequent days.
- Model is overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true values are rising or volatile.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of true price drops, particularly in the final 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonality or policy-driven volatility (e.g., ETS auction dates, regulatory changes) in the final 10–15 days.
